req.title: Create new post
req.statement: The system shall insert a new post attributed to the logged-in user when POST /create receives a title and body, then redirect to /.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /create must insert a new post attributed to the logged-in user and redirect to /. I design: (1) a positive EP test verifying the happy path — valid title+body yields 302 to / and the post appears in the DB; (2) a negative NEG test verifying that missing title returns no redirect and flashes an error; (3) a BVA boundary test with a single-character title (minimum non-empty boundary) to confirm it is accepted; (4) a DT test verifying that an unauthenticated POST /create is rejected with a redirect to /auth/login (not inserted); (5) an STC test verifying the post is attributed to the correct author_id in the database. Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill operator-flip and constant-bump mutations.

tests.name: test_create_post_valid_title_and_body_redirects_to_index
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User Rahul (id=1) is logged in via POST /auth/login
actions: POST /create with title='My Test Post' and body='Some body text'
expected: New post row with title='My Test Post' exists in the database with author_id=1
trace: R-FLASKR-015: POST /create with valid title and body inserts post and redirects to /
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in as Rahul (id=1)
lr = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert lr.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {lr.status_code}'

# POST /create with valid data
r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'My Test Post', 'body': 'Some body text'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/', f'Expected redirect to /, got {r.headers["Location"]}'

# Verify post inserted in DB with correct author
with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute("SELECT title, body, author_id FROM post WHERE id = 21").fetchone()
    assert row is not None, 'Post with id=21 not found'
    assert row['title'] == 'My Test Post'
    assert row['body'] == 'Some body text'
    assert row['author_id'] == 1

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_create_post_missing_title_does_not_insert_and_shows_error
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
actions: POST /create with empty title and non-empty body
expected: No new post row inserted (post count remains 20)
trace: R-FLASKR-015: missing title triggers error path; no DB insert; no redirect
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

lr = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
assert lr.status_code == 302

# POST /create with empty title
r = client.post('/create', data={'title': '', 'body': 'Some body text'})
assert r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200, got {r.status_code}'
assert b'Title is required.' in r.data, 'Error message not found in response'

# Verify no new post was inserted
with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    count = db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post").fetchone()[0]
    assert count == 20, f'Expected 20 posts, got {count}'
    row21 = db.execute("SELECT id FROM post WHERE id = 21").fetchone()
    assert row21 is None, 'Post id=21 should not exist'

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_create_post_unauthenticated_redirects_to_login_no_insert
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
No user is logged in (anonymous session)
actions: POST /create with valid title and body without prior login
expected: No new post row inserted (count remains 20)
trace: R-FLASKR-015: login_required decorator must block unauthenticated POST /create
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# No login — anonymous request
r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'Unauthorized Post', 'body': 'body'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', (
    f'Expected /auth/login, got {r.headers["Location"]}'
)

# Confirm no post was inserted
with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    count = db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post").fetchone()[0]
    assert count == 20, f'Expected 20 posts, got {count}'
    row = db.execute(
        "SELECT id FROM post WHERE title = 'Unauthorized Post'"
    ).fetchone()
    assert row is None, 'Unauthorized post must not be inserted'

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_create_post_attributed_to_logged_in_user_not_another
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User Ishaan (id=3) is logged in (not Rahul id=1)
actions: POST /create with title='Ishaan Post' and body='authored by Ishaan'
expected: Inserted post has author_id=3 (Ishaan), NOT author_id=1 (Rahul)
trace: R-FLASKR-015: post must be attributed to the logged-in user; catches author_id mutation
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

# Log in as Ishaan (id=3)
lr = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
assert lr.status_code == 302, f'Login failed: {lr.status_code}'

r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'Ishaan Post', 'body': 'authored by Ishaan'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    row = db.execute("SELECT author_id, title FROM post WHERE id = 21").fetchone()
    assert row is not None, 'Post id=21 not found'
    assert row['title'] == 'Ishaan Post'
    assert row['author_id'] == 3, f'Expected author_id=3, got {row["author_id"]}'
    assert row['author_id'] != 1, 'Post must not be attributed to Rahul'

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_create_post_index_page_shows_new_post_title
preconditions: App initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
actions: POST /create with title='Diya Unique Title 99' and body='body'
GET / to verify the new post appears
expected: GET / returns 200 and contains b'Diya Unique Title 99'
Total post count in DB is exactly 21
trace: R-FLASKR-015: after insert, index page must display the new post title
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

lr = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Diya', 'password': 'cloud'})
assert lr.status_code == 302

r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'Diya Unique Title 99', 'body': 'body'})
assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302, got {r.status_code}'
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

# Follow redirect to index
index_r = client.get('/')
assert index_r.status_code == 200, f'Expected 200, got {index_r.status_code}'
assert b'Diya Unique Title 99' in index_r.data, 'New post title not found on index page'

# Verify exact count
with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    count = db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post").fetchone()[0]
    assert count == 21, f'Expected 21 posts, got {count}'

os.unlink(path)
